title: Projective affine charts after elementary etale source and base neighbourhoods
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and suppose $F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. There exist affine schemes $Y,S'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], points $y\in Y$ and $s'\in S'$, and morphisms $g:Y\to X$, $q:Y\to S'$, $e:S'\to S$ with $f\circ g=e\circ q$, $g(y)=x$ and $q(y)=s'$, such that both $(Y,y)\to(X,x)$ and $(S',s')\to(S,s)$ are elementary etale neighbourhoods: their morphisms are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and induce isomorphisms $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(y)$ and $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s')$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Moreover $\Gamma(Y,g^*F)$ is projective over $\Gamma(S',\mathcal O_{S'})$ through $q$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. No finite-generation hypothesis over this base ring is imposed.

proof.text: Choose affine opens $V\ni s$ and $W\ni x$ with $W\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Put $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)$, $B=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)$ and $M=\Gamma(W,F)$. The map $A\to B$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], and $M$ is finitely presented over $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-affine-sections]. The counit of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identifies $F|_W$ with $\widetilde M$. For $w\in W$ with primes $\mathfrak q_w\subset B$ and $\mathfrak p_w\subset A$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] identify the module stalk with $M_{\mathfrak q_w}$ and the base stalk with $A_{\mathfrak p_w}$, respecting the scalar action (both send a section to its germ). By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization], $M_{\mathfrak q_w}$ is flat over $A_{\mathfrak p_w}$ exactly when it is flat over $A$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-openness-of-flatness] gives an open $E\subseteq W$ consisting precisely of the points where $F$ is flat over $S$. The hypothesis gives $x\in E$.

source.place: Tag 05ID, proposition-finite-presentation-flat-at-point, first sentence; affine proof of Tag 0399 (more-morphisms theorem-openness-flatness) using Algebra Tag 00RC.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U\ni x$ inside $E$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Keep $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, replace $B$ by $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O)$, and put $M=\Gamma(U,F)$. Again [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-affine-sections] give that $A\to B$ and the $B$-module $M$ are finitely presented. In particular $B$ is generated by finitely many algebra generators over $A$, and the cokernel presentation of $M$ supplies finitely many module generators. Write $\mathfrak q\subset B$, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ for $x,s$. Every stalk of $F|_U$ is flat over $V$: the open inclusion $V\subset S$ identifies its local rings with those of $S$. The restrictions retain quasi-coherence and finite presentation since their local presentations are the same on the smaller opens.

source.place: Tag 05ID, first sentence: replace X by a flat neighbourhood; choose affine source and target charts before the devissage construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-complete-algebra-devissage-etale-existence] to $A\to B,M,\mathfrak q$. Obtain a commutative square with rings $A_0,B_0$, primes $\mathfrak p_0,\mathfrak q_0$, etale spectrum maps $e_0:T_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0\to V$ and $g_0:Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0\to U$, and both specified residue-field isomorphisms. Let $q_0:Y_0\to T_0$ be the fourth map. Its marked points map to $x,s$ and to each other by the prime contractions in the cited statement. Put $H=g_0^*(F|_U)$ and $N_0=\Gamma(Y_0,H)$. The affine counit [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] identify $H$ with $\widetilde{B_0\otimes_B M}$ and $N_0$ with $B_0\otimes_B M$. The interchange $b_0\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes b_0$, inverse $m\otimes b_0\mapsto b_0\otimes m$, identifies this with the module in the cited existence theorem. Therefore $N_0/B_0/A_0$ has a complete algebra devissage over $\mathfrak p_0$.

source.place: Tag 05ID, application of proposition-existence-complete-at-x (05HR) and remark-same-notion (05I0); their algebraic reformulation is Tag 05I1 (lemma-existence-algebra).

proof.text: The map $U\to V$ is locally of finite presentation: the affine finite presentation in step 2 gives a single chart in the definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] with $P$ locally of finite presentation to the square in step 3. Its two horizontal maps are etale, so $q_0$ is locally of finite presentation. Since $Y_0,T_0$ are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives that $A_0\to B_0$ is finitely presented. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] and [lem-pc-tensor-pullback-finite-presentation], $H$ is quasi-coherent and finitely presented. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-affine-sections] makes $N_0$ finitely presented over $B_0$. We have imposed no finite-presentation condition on $N_0$ over $A_0$.

source.place: Tag 05ID: finite presentation hypotheses for the final application of Tag 05IB; source and target etale permanence.

proof.text: The etale map $g_0$ is flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. At every $z\in Y_0$, [lem-trf-relative-flatness-source-cover] applied to $g_0:Y_0\to U$ over $V$ and $F|_U$ shows that $H$ is flat over $V$ at $z$, using step 2. Put $t=q_0(z)$ and $v=e_0(t)$. The stalk $H_z$ is an $\mathcal O_{T_0,t}$-module through $q_0$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness] to the etale $e_0:T_0\to V$ and this module: flatness over $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ implies flatness over $\mathcal O_{T_0,t}$. Consequently $H$ is flat over $T_0$ at every point. By [lem-pc-affine-chart-relative-flat-criterion] on the whole affine $Y_0$ over the affine $T_0$, $N_0$ is flat over $A_0$. This checks flatness over the new base without asserting that the square is cartesian.

source.place: Tag 05ID, flat-permanence (Morphisms Tag 02JZ, lemma-flat-permanence) and lemma-etale-flat-up-down (05B9), using its stalk form 05BA (lemma-etale-flat-up-down-local-ring).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-complete-algebra-devissage-projective-localization] to $A_0\to B_0$, $N_0$, and $\mathfrak p_0$. Its hypotheses are finite presentation of the algebra and of the source module (step 4), flatness over $A_0$ (step 5), and the complete devissage (step 3). Obtain $a\in A_0\setminus\mathfrak p_0$ such that $(N_0)_a=N_0\otimes_{A_0}(A_0)_a$ is projective over $(A_0)_a$. The result allows arbitrary rank. In particular it requires neither finite generation nor finite presentation over $A_0$.

Let $b$ be the image of $a$ in $B_0$. Define $S'=D(a)\subset T_0$ and $Y=D(b)\subset Y_0$. They are affine with rings $(A_0)_a,(B_0)_b$ by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion]. The restriction $q:Y\to S'$ exists because the inverse image of $D(a)$ is $D(b)$. For the quasi-coherent $H$, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change] gives $\Gamma(Y,H|_Y)=N_0\otimes_{B_0}(B_0)_b$. This is canonically $N_0\otimes_{A_0}(A_0)_a$: both are the module of fractions $n/a^k$, with $n\otimes(c/b^k)\mapsto cn/a^k$ and $n/a^k\mapsto n\otimes 1/b^k$. These maps are well defined by the fraction relations and inverse on the displayed generators. For the composite $g:Y\to Y_0\to U\to X$, [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition] identifies $g^*F$ with $H|_Y$ (pullback by an open inclusion is restriction by its tensor formula). Hence step 6 is exactly the required projectivity of $\Gamma(Y,g^*F)$ through $q$.

source.place: Tag 05ID, final standard-open replacement of the base, and its inverse image in the affine source.

proof.text: Since $a\notin\mathfrak p_0$ and $\mathfrak q_0\cap A_0=\mathfrak p_0$, also $b\notin\mathfrak q_0$. Thus both marked points remain in $S',Y$. The maps $Y\to Y_0$, $U\to X$, $S'\to T_0$, and $V\to S$ are open immersions; they are etale, and their composites with $g_0,e_0$ are etale by clauses (1)--(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The new principal-open localizations preserve the marked residue fields by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], clauses (1)--(3); the initial open restrictions $U\subset X,V\subset S$ also have identical local rings at their points, since the neighbourhoods contained in an open form a cofinal system for its stalk. Composing these isomorphisms with the residue isomorphisms of step 3 gives $\kappa(x)\cong\kappa(y)$ and $\kappa(s)\cong\kappa(s')$. The square remains commutative by restriction of the square of step 3. These maps and points give every clause of the statement.

source.place: Tag 05ID, pointed elementary-etale diagram after the final standard-open replacement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q58-d29b6b57e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 8 steps and all 24 cited statements in full and checked them against Stacks flat.tex 05ID (l.3286-3340) and the tags it uses (05I1, 05IB, 02JZ, 05BA, 00RC/0399). There are no new nodes and no repair note, so this is the first proof of an imported item, not a re-split. The statement matches 05ID exactly: locally finitely presented f, a quasi-coherent finitely presented F, F_x flat over O_{S,s}, two affine elementary étale neighbourhoods, and projective sections with arbitrary rank. Nothing is weakened. Steps: (1) 01TQ, 01PC, the tilde counit, 01HV(6)/(7) and 00HT(2) reduce openness of flatness to 00RC. (2) Shrink to an affine U inside the flat locus. (3) 05I1 gives the dévissage, and 01I9 identifies N_0 with B_0⊗_B M; the dévissage def allows transfer along this isomorphism. (4) The source-target property in the square fa=bh makes q_0 lfp, then 01TQ, 01BG/01BQ and 01PC give finite presentation over B_0 only. (5) 02JZ, then 05BA, then the affine chart criterion give N_0 flat over A_0 without assuming the square is cartesian. (6) 05IB hypotheses all checked. (7)-(8) Principal opens via 01I3/01LN/0097, residue fields via 00E3, étaleness via 02GP/02GN. Edge cases checked: X empty, F=0 (length-0 dévissage), non-closed points, non-Noetherian base, infinite rank. Duplicates: lem-trf-flat-algebra-etale-projective-neighborhood is only the structure-sheaf case with global flatness, and the parent 05ME node cites the item. No cycle in the proof_dep closures. Batch 5: all five flagged citations are generic Stacks algebra or permanence lemmas (05I1, 05IB, 02JZ, 05BA, and smooth composition reached through the source-target node); their closures reach no nt-*, trace or Poincaré node. Accepted as tools, as are the declared off-route sk-i-curve-zero tool_uses. Advisory: the tool_uses 'why' for relative-flatness-source-cover says 047C where 02JZ is meant (cosmetic). No SGA source is used.

lean.statement: theorem exists_projective_affine_etale_source_chart {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFinitePresentation] (x : X) (hflat : Module.Flat (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (f.stalkMap x).hom).obj ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).obj F))) : ∃ (Y S' : Scheme.{u}) (y : Y) (s' : S') (g : Y ⟶ X) (q : Y ⟶ S') (e : S' ⟶ S), IsAffine Y ∧ IsAffine S' ∧ g ≫ f = q ≫ e ∧ g y = x ∧ q y = s' ∧ Etale g ∧ IsIso (g.residueFieldMap y) ∧ Etale e ∧ IsIso (e.residueFieldMap s') ∧ @Module.Projective Γ(S', ⊤) _ Γ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g).obj F, ⊤) _ (Module.compHom _ q.appTop.hom)
